subject: Clearline: Request for key custody transcripts and rotation artifacts
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearline.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: key custody transcripts + rotation artifacts for security review

Hi Marissa,

As part of Clearline's onboarding security review (SIG + SOC2 appendix), we need to collect artifacts that demonstrate how Redwood manages customer KEKs and wrapping/unwrapping events across your KMS/HSM stack. Specifically, can you provide:  

- Event-level rotation logs (wrap/unwrap) for the tenant scope for the last 6 months (format preference: ndjson or CSV).
- HSM attestation/cert of seal for the current HSM appliance(s).
- Operator access matrix and recent operator session summaries.
- A brief narrative describing how rotation is triggered, how wrap keys are derived (KEK/DEK flow), and where retention snapshots are stored.

We cannot accept any unredacted customer payloads; event metadata only is fine (timestamps, operator id, event type, key identifier, wrapped key fingerprint). Would it be possible to get these files by EOD Mon (11/30)?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Staff Security Engineer, Clearline Financial
security@clearline.com

(Please reply with an S3/Drive link and list of attachment filenames.)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearline.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: key custody transcripts + rotation artifacts for security review

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver those artifacts; a couple quick clarifying items before we package them:  

1) For "event-level rotation logs" — do you need raw keystore logs with one-line JSON per event (ndjson), or is an audited CSV with the same fields acceptable? We can provide both but want to be sure on preferred format.
2) For HSM attestation, are you expecting the vendor-signed attestation PEM and a checksum, or a full attestation bundle (PEM + chain + HSM serial + firmware manifest)?
3) On redaction: we will strip any customer payloads and only include the metadata fields you mentioned; we can additionally truncate any identifiers to the first 8 chars if that helps with privacy.

I'll assemble a proposed manifest and drop the artifacts into a locked Drive folder (and include checksums). If that timeline works, we will aim to deliver by end-of-day Monday (11/30).

Looping in Neha for the technical artifact pack and myself for the manifest.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

(Attachment: initial-artifact-manifest.txt)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: key custody transcripts + rotation artifacts for security review

Marissa — thanks. NDJSON is preferred for event-level logs, we ingest line-delimited JSON into our pipeline. For HSM attestation we need the vendor-signed attestation PEM plus the firmware manifest (if available).

Two more constraints from our side:  
- Do not include any user/customer PII or full ciphertext blobs in the artifact files. Metadata only as noted.
- We require event timestamps in UTC and a field called "event_id" that can be used for cross-referencing.

If you can deliver a read-only Drive link or an S3 presigned URL with 7-day expiry, that will work. Appreciate the help — if anything blocks delivery, let us know and we'll adjust the review schedule.

Alex

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearline.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: key custody transcripts + rotation artifacts for security review

Hi Alex — quick technical note on the artifacts we'll deliver and how we've prepared them:  

Summary of artifacts (attached):
- redwood-kms-rotation-events-202605-202611.ndjson  (line-delimited JSON; fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id_masked, key_id, event_type, operator_id_masked, wrapped_key_fingerprint, rotation_trigger)
- redwood-hsm-attestation-serial-20261129.pem  (vendor-signed attestation; includes serial + firmware manifest)
- redwood-access-matrix-operators.csv  (operator id, role, last_auth_ts, azure_oauth_subject mask)
- soc2-appendix-kms-control-mapping.pdf  (mapping of SOC2 control IDs to Redwood KMS/HSM processes)

Redaction approach:  
- Tenant identifiers are masked to the first 8 characters with a consistent salt so you can cross-reference within the pack but not recover tenant data.
- No ciphertext payloads or customer data are present. Only metadata and wrapped-key fingerprints (sha256 truncated).
- Timestamps are in ISO-8601 UTC.

Additional notes on rotation process (short):
- Rotation window: we run scheduled KEK rotations monthly; emergency rotations are triggered via an operator-run canary job and recorded as event_type="manual_rotation".
- Wrap/unwrap flow: DEKs are derived per-tenant, wrapped under a KEK in the HSM. KEKs are wrapped with a hardware-protected master key; HSM enforces wrap/unwrap and logs operator identity + operation id.
- Audit export: event-level logs are exported from our audit pipeline as ndjson and signed (SHA256) before packaging. The archive includes a signed manifest with checksums.

Delivery plan: I'll upload the package to a Drive folder and send a read-only link with checksums by EOD Monday (11/30). If you prefer S3 presigned URLs instead, tell us and we can provide those.

(Attached: artifact-checksums.txt, packaging-manifest.json)

—Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
